newsitem.title: PERU: PERU SAYS 13 FIRMS KEEN ON ELECTRICITY CONCESSION.
newsitem.headline: PERU SAYS 13 FIRMS KEEN ON ELECTRICITY CONCESSION.

text.p: The government said Friday 13 firms, including companies from the United States and Europe, were interested in the concession to construct a $250 million electricity link between Peru's north and southern grids.

"There is a lot of interest in this concession, because it will join the whole (electric) energy system of Peru, north to south," Rene Cornejo, from the state privatization committee, said in an interview.
Cornejo added more firms would likley show interest in the concession before its planned November auction.
The concession winner is expected to operate the concession early 1998.
The government forecasts Peru's electricity demand will grow 5.5 percent annually for the next ten years, prompting a wave of concessions to extend the country's electricity network.
